summary: Published a week before the May 2023 general election with Pita Limjaroenrat as the guest, and the comment section stops being an entertainment thread and becomes a campaign one. Roughly half the comments are explicit endorsements — he should be the next prime minister, vote Move Forward, orange emoji strings — and the channel's own pinned comment simply says don't forget to vote. A significant cluster thanks the channel for making politics feel close to young viewers who would not watch a political interview, framing the hosts as a conduit rather than commentators. A third, much later wave arrived after 14 February 2026 when Goy revealed her relationship with him: commenters confess they came back from Valentine's Day and re-read her admiring gaze in the episode as the beginning of it. A smaller cluster carries hindsight regret that he never became prime minister. At 11,251 comments this is the most-commented post on the channel.

audience_signals: A non-entertainment guest booked at the right political moment produced the channel's most-commented post ever — 11,251 comments, roughly double the next highest
The audience credits the flirt-interview format with lowering the barrier to political content for young viewers, which is a genuine positioning asset the channel does not currently claim
The episode gained a second life three years later: the hosts' real relationship turned it into a romance origin story and drove a fresh rewatch wave with no new production cost
Partisan association is permanent and explicit in this thread — worth knowing before pitching brand-sensitive sponsors against the back catalogue
The format travels far outside entertainment: the same questions applied to a party leader produced substantive answers viewers described as considered
content_requests: More political and serious guests in the same format
A follow-up episode with the same guest
Keep using the format to bring civic topics to a young audience
